questions.prompt:
Part (a): Test whether \(A=\begin{pmatrix}14&4i\\-4i&14\end{pmatrix}\) is Hermitian.
Part (b): Prove that every complex square matrix has a unique Hermitian plus anti-Hermitian decomposition.
questions.answer:
Part (a)
We need to complete the requested calculation or proof.
Method: Apply the stated mathematical method and simplify each step.
Conjugating and transposing gives
\[A^\dagger=\begin{pmatrix}14&4i\\-4i&14\end{pmatrix}=A.\]
Final answer: \(A\) is Hermitian.

Part (b)
We need to complete the requested calculation or proof.
Method: Apply the stated mathematical method and simplify each step.
Set
\[H=\frac12(A+A^\dagger),\qquad K=\frac12(A-A^\dagger).\]
Then \(H^\dagger=H\), \(K^\dagger=-K\), and \(A=H+K\). If \(A=H_1+K_1\), taking adjoints and adding or subtracting recovers the same formulas.
Final answer: \(A=(A+A^\dagger)/2+(A-A^\dagger)/2\), uniquely.

questions.prompt:
Part (a): Calculate the quadratic form of \(A=\operatorname{diag}(15,5)\) at \(\mathbf x=(1,2)^{\mathsf T}\).
Part (b): Prove that every eigenvalue of a Hermitian matrix is real.
questions.answer:
Part (a)
We need to complete the requested calculation or proof.
Method: Apply the stated mathematical method and simplify each step.
\[\mathbf x^{\mathsf T}A\mathbf x=15(1)^2+5(2)^2=35.\]
Final answer: \(\mathbf x^{\mathsf T}A\mathbf x=35\).

Part (b)
We need to complete the requested calculation or proof.
Method: Apply the stated mathematical method and simplify each step.
If \(A\mathbf v=\lambda\mathbf v\), then
\[\mathbf v^\dagger A\mathbf v=\lambda\mathbf v^\dagger\mathbf v.\]
Taking conjugates and using \(A^\dagger=A\) gives the same left side equal to \(\overline\lambda\mathbf v^\dagger\mathbf v\). Since \(\mathbf v\ne0\), \(\lambda=\overline\lambda\).
Final answer: Every Hermitian eigenvalue is real.

questions.prompt:
Part (a): Test whether \(Q(x,y)=16x^2+1y^2\) is positive definite.
Part (b): Prove that a unitary matrix preserves the complex inner product.
questions.answer:
Part (a)
We need to complete the requested calculation or proof.
Method: Apply the stated mathematical method and simplify each step.
Both coefficients satisfy \(16>0\) and \(1>0\), so \(Q(x,y)>0\) whenever \((x,y)\ne(0,0)\).
Final answer: \(Q\) is positive definite.

Part (b)
We need to complete the requested calculation or proof.
Method: Apply the stated mathematical method and simplify each step.
For \(U^\dagger U=I\),
\[\langle U\mathbf x,U\mathbf y\rangle=(U\mathbf x)^\dagger U\mathbf y=\mathbf x^\dagger U^\dagger U\mathbf y=\mathbf x^\dagger\mathbf y.\]
Final answer: \(\langle U\mathbf x,U\mathbf y\rangle=\langle\mathbf x,\mathbf y\rangle\).
